editorial:
Imagine an adorable elderly couple who think they are just following a helpful guide from the government to stay safe. You get to know these two sweet people as they happily build a backyard shelter, thinking that a nuclear war will be just like the old days of World War II. The vibe is weirdly cozy at first, but you can feel a sense of dread building up because you know something they don't. It is a heartbreaking look at how innocent people can trust the wrong instructions while the world around them is about to end.

What really hits home is the acting and the way the movie slows down to show their love for each other. The pacing is a bit slow, but that makes the ending feel much heavier. If you like stories that make you think about the world, you will love this. Just make sure you have some tissues nearby before you start.
endingExplained: The couple finishes their shelter, but it is not strong enough to stop a real nuclear blast. When the bombs finally drop, the shockwave destroys their home and their shelter instantly. The final scenes show them suffering from radiation sickness. They hold each other and talk about their love until they both pass away. It is a sad ending that shows the government pamphlets were useless and the war was far worse than they imagined.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories that tug at the heartstrings.
